To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

in potato tubers the majority of the flux control in sucrose to starch conversion is in the transfer of ATP between the cytosolic and plastidial compartments and that this control is exerted by the ATP/ADP translocase, and that in leaves the majority of the metabolic control in sucrose-to-starch conversion is in the plastidial phosphoglucan metabolism, and that this control resides in the reactions catalyzed by phosphoglucan isomerase and AGP

the majority of control on the rate of starch accumulation resides in the transfer between the cytosolic and amyloplast compartments, and that this control is mediated via the adenylate translocators.

the control of starch synthesis in potato tuber amyloplasts resides predominantly with the plastidial adenylatetranslocator, and the control of sucrose synthesis is predominantly with the sucrose synthase reaction, and that these two reactions together account for approximately 90% of the control of the sucrose-starch pathway in potato tubers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the regulation of the sucrose/starch pathway in potato tubers.
understanding how the potato tuber converts sucrose into starch.
the study of metabolic control and the role of regulation in metabolic networks.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the potato tuber provides an attractive model system to study the regulation of the conversion from sucrose to starch.
the control of sucrose to amylose conversion in potato tubers is a highly regulated process.
sucrose is converted into starch by a series of enzyme-catalysed reactions that are controlled by both the mass action ratio of the enzymes and the distribution of control within the pathway.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
control analysis is a powerful tool for the elucidation of metabolic pathways.
control of sucrose to hexose conversion in potato tubers is largely in the cytosol, with the control of the conversion of hexose to starch residing in the plastid.

metabolic control analysis has been used successfully to determine the distribution of control on the conversion of sucrale to starch in the potato tuber, and this information has been used to generate hypotheses regarding the control of this important metabolic pathway.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a comprehensive understanding of the regulation and control of a metabolic pathway requires the integration of several different types of data.

metabolic control analysis and the determination of the mass action ratio of the enzymes of a metabolic pathway can be used in a complementary fashion to provide a comprehensive description of the control and regulation of that pathway.
the control of flux in a pathway is distributed across the entire pathway and that the control is not necessarily located at the rate limiting steps.
